expectations.text: Report identifies that the root defect is at write time (signup stores email as-typed).

Why 3: 'Signup passes the email through untouched and `insert` stores whatever it receives; nothing in the codebase normalises email.' expectations.text: Skim test: the headline states what broke, the root cause, and the recommended fix in one sentence, and the first sentence of each section carries its claim; no first sentence is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: The Headline is a five-sentence paragraph, not one sentence; the H1 title carries only the symptom. Its first sentence, 'Search is not the bug; it is the first place the bug was noticed.', is a teaser that withholds the cause and fix (both appear only in sentences 2 and 5). Section leads also miss the bar: Timeline opens with the qualifier 'The fixture has no version history, so `git log` cannot name an introducing change.'; Symptom and scope, Classification, Assumptions and Fix proposals open with bullets or a bold label rather than a claim sentence. Siblings ('All four callers share `db.find_by_email`, so all four misbehave on a case mismatch') is the one section lead that does carry its claim.

notes: The content assertions are well chosen for this bait prompt and the run earned every one of them with verified work (probes, scratch-copy experiments, accurate citations, fixture left byte-identical). Two gaps: no assertion checks that the file:line citations are accurate, so a report with three hallucinated locations passes assertion 8 (I verified them by hand here); and nothing checks that outputs/fixture was left unmodified, which the prompt demands and the skill treats as a hard rule. The report's strongest discriminating finding, that the requested one-liner cannot even be written in search.py because `u` is out of scope, is only indirectly covered by assertion 2. Assertion 3's 'at write time' wording is slightly looser than the report's actual root ('no canonical form, applied inconsistently on write and read'), which a stricter grader could read as a near miss; consider rewording to 'names the as-typed store on signup as part of the root'. The two failures are both prose-form checks the old skill never asked for, so they measure the writing rules rather than RCA quality, which is exactly what the new/old comparison needs.
